counterfactual_missing_items: R1 lacks the decisive FH-loss and FH-variant evidence, so it under-specifies the FHIR-deficiency subtype.
R4 names a syndrome but does not account for the ovarian primary and smooth-muscle spindle cell histology of the leiomyoma.
R6 is only supported by the imaging-suggested bilateral breast mass; it has no raw permit for the pelvic mass or FH-defect.
decisive_items: Findings were suggestive of an ovarian primary
pathogenic variant in the FH gene (FHc.999C > A p.Cys333Ter)
response.rationale: C1 is the most composite diagnosis: the ovarian primary and smooth-muscle phenotype locate the lump as ovarian leiomyoma, while FHIR loss and the pathogenic kind provide the specific fumarate-hydratase-deficient cause. R4 is a reasonable genetic-level interpretation but overgeneralizes to the syndrome and omits the ovarian pathology; R1 lacks the FHIR evidence; and R6 addresses only fibroadenomas.

rejected.why: Accurate at the anatomy/histology level but omits the FHIR deficiency and germline FHIR confirmed by IHC/genetic case, leaving subtype
It only reflects the suspected breast fibroadenomas and cannot account for the ovarian spindle-cell leyoma or FHIR loss.
